text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing tail latency step-ups on the p0 serving cluster after the matmul runtime change this morning. 50th pct fine but 99th jumps around 2-3x.
arjun: Which nodes/trace do we have? nsys capture? stack?
maya: Pushed an nsys capture to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/nsys/2067894200_matmul_queuehog.qzst. Quick findings: long stretches of KERNEL_QUEUE stalls, then batches hit a cuBLASLt workspace allocation failure and we see fallbacks to the default algo which is much slower. snippet from runtime log: 
```
E 10:12:04 cublasLt: workspaceAlloc failed (size=2457600) -> falling back to algo idx -1
W 10:12:04 gemm: fallback to algo 0 (expected latency +120ms)
```
liv: Hmm. Did the shape distribution change? Or did algo probing start preferring algo with big workspace?
sara: Shape distro skewed toward longer seqs during the spike (requests had max_seq=2048 for ~10s) and we had a KV cache warmup burst, so more concurrent long inferences. That increases aggregate workspace pressure. Perfetto timelines show memcpy peaks aligning with those queuing periods.
perf-bot: nsys summary: 26% time in cublasLt kernels, 18% stalled on kernel_launch_queue, 42% of cublasLt calls used fallback algo 0, median workspace_needed=1.8MB, 95th=6.2MB.
arjun: Did we recently change the cublasLt probe policy? I faintly remember a heuristic tweak to pick higher-throughput algos even if they need more workspace.
maya: Yes — the probe tweak in #PR-1187 nudged selection toward higher-throughput algos for medium batch shapes. On p0 this is causing collisions with other concurrent allocs.
liv: Short-term mitigation: clamp the effective batch_size for sequences >1024 or cap the probed workspace size. Also we can pre-allocate a reserved workspace slab for matmuls to avoid fragmentation.
sara: I ran a microbenchmark on a dev node: toggling slab_alloc to true drops fallback rate from 42% -> 6% and 99th latency by ~28%, throughput down ~6% under peak.
arjun: Good. Can we do a quick config flip in Dedicated fleet for the affected pool? Try slab_alloc + max_concurrent_matmuls=16.
maya: Did that just now on a canary subset. Tail improved ~30% but throughput dipped as expected. We need a better long-term fix.
liv: Long-term plan: add a per-shape algo cache (LRU) keyed by (m,n,k,seq_len) with recorded workspace requirement + chosen algo. On workspaceAlloc failure, check cache for compatible algo before falling back to algo 0. Also surface probe stats in the console so deploys can see workspace risk.
sara: I'll prototype the LRU + pre-probe warmup. Quick perf command I used: 
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas --output=tmp /opt/redwood/bin/matmul_probe --shape 2048x512x512 --iters 500
```
perf-bot: Created ticket INF-4382 and linked the nsys capture + perf logs.
arjun: Sounds good. maya/sara/liv — please coordinate a PR with tests that validate fallback behavior (simulate alloc failure path) and add a rollout plan. Include canary metrics.
maya: Will do. assigning to sara for prototype and to liv for design doc. I'll leave the canary with slab_alloc for now. :thumbsup:
